nodes.name: Security Office
nodes.summary: Appoint a Security Director and open the Security branch.
nodes.why: You cannot see where the trouble is. This adds the danger meter and the sector view, and everything else on the security side depends on it.

nodes.name: Welfare
nodes.summary: Appoint a Counsellor and run behavioural and alcohol programs.
nodes.why: Unmet needs are the root cause of most misconduct. The needs report tells you which one, and the programs give you something to do about it.

nodes.name: Medical
nodes.summary: Hire medics, build a clinic and a mortuary, treat addiction.
nodes.why: Without a medic an injured inmate bleeds out and an overdose is fatal. Deaths are a failure condition.

nodes.name: Education
nodes.summary: Build classrooms, engage instructors, run the education programs.
nodes.why: Literacy and vocational certificates are the two largest single reductions to re-offending you can buy.

nodes.name: Legal
nodes.summary: Appoint a Legal Officer and open the Legal branch.
nodes.why: Legal work changes what the rules let you do: smaller cells, longer sanctions, and a way to survive one game over.

nodes.name: Works
nodes.summary: Appoint a Works Manager and open the Works branch.
nodes.why: Cleaning, grounds and inmate labour all sit behind this. Dirt is the quietest way a prison goes wrong.

nodes.name: Finance
nodes.summary: Appoint a Finance Officer, open the finance reports and the Finance branch.
nodes.why: Until this completes you are guessing at your daily net. Insolvency is a failure condition and it arrives without warning.

nodes.name: Standing Orders
nodes.summary: Set punishment policy per misconduct type and meal quantity and variety.
nodes.why: Without it every punishment is manual and every meal is the cheapest option. Meal quality is a direct lever on misconduct.

nodes.name: Delegation
nodes.summary: Schedule posts and programs, and route kitchens and laundries by hand.
nodes.why: Automatic nearest-first routing sends meals across the prison when a closer mess hall is full. This lets you fix it.

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.summary: Cameras, monitor banks and phone taps.
nodes.why: Officers only see what they walk past. Cameras hold fog of war open in the places you cannot afford to post someone.

nodes.name: Posts
nodes.summary: Assign staff to a place and a time window rather than a wander area.
nodes.why: Three officers in the mess hall at mealtimes stops more fights than thirty officers wandering at random.

nodes.name: Intelligence
nodes.summary: Recruit informants and read the contraband market.
nodes.why: You are searching blind. Informants tell you which rooms are leaking and where the stashes are.

nodes.name: Patrols
nodes.summary: Waypoint routes walked in a loop, with optional time windows.
nodes.why: A predictable circuit covers a corridor with one officer instead of three.

nodes.name: Canine
nodes.summary: Dog handlers, patrol dogs and kennels.
nodes.why: Dogs are the only passive detector for odorous contraband, and the only reliable way to find tunnels before they reach the fence.

nodes.name: Automation
nodes.summary: Door control desks, timers and logic for sally ports.
nodes.why: Every locked door an officer has to open by hand is an officer not doing anything else.

nodes.name: Armoury
nodes.summary: Build an armoury and hire armed officers.
nodes.why: Armed officers end riots. They also make the armoury the most valuable room in the prison to steal from.

nodes.name: Stun Devices
nodes.summary: Certified officers may carry a stun device.
nodes.why: A stun device ends a fight without the injury, and injuries reclassify inmates upward.

nodes.name: General Issue Stun
nodes.summary: Issue stun devices to every officer without individual certification.
nodes.why: Certifying officers one at a time costs classroom hours you would rather spend on inmates.

nodes.name: Protective Vests
nodes.summary: Halve the damage staff take.
nodes.why: Staff deaths cost eight morale points each for a week, and morale drives search effectiveness and bribes.

nodes.name: Watchtowers
nodes.summary: Towers and marksmen overlooking the yard and the perimeter.
nodes.why: A tower suppresses everything it can see, which is cheaper than posting officers across an open yard.

nodes.name: Compact Cells
nodes.summary: Remove the minimum size requirement on cells.
nodes.why: Cells are the largest single line in your construction budget. Smaller ones grade worse, so this is a deliberate trade.

nodes.name: Indefinite Sanctions
nodes.summary: Hold an inmate in isolation without a fixed end time.
nodes.why: Some inmates never stop. This works, and it destroys their reform grade, which shows up in your re-offending rate.

nodes.name: Capital Cases
nodes.summary: Accept condemned inmates.
nodes.why: They pay the most per day of any category. Getting one wrong is its own failure condition.

nodes.name: Reduced Liability
nodes.summary: Cut the cost of incidents, injuries and deaths.
nodes.why: A bad week currently costs you twice: once in the incident and once in the payout.

nodes.name: Retainer
nodes.summary: Standing legal cover against claims arising from your prison.
nodes.why: At scale the claims never stop arriving. A retainer turns a variable cost into a fixed one.

nodes.name: Counsel
nodes.summary: Cancel one failure condition, once.
nodes.why: It is expensive and it works exactly once. Buy it when the countdown has already started.

nodes.name: Inmate Labour
nodes.summary: Assign inmates to kitchen, laundry, workshop, library, mail and commissary work.
nodes.why: Working inmates misbehave less, reform faster and cost you nothing in wages.

nodes.name: Sanitation
nodes.summary: Hire cleaners and build supply closets.
nodes.why: Dirt drives the environment need for everyone in the room, and it rises whether or not you are watching.

nodes.name: Grounds
nodes.summary: Hire groundskeepers and plant a grove.
nodes.why: Outdoor dirt is nobody's job until you hire for it, and the grove turns idle land into timber.

nodes.name: Tax Relief
nodes.summary: Reduce the daily tax charge.
nodes.why: Tax scales with your income, so this is worth more the better the prison is doing.

nodes.name: Offshore Structure
nodes.summary: Remove the daily tax charge entirely.
nodes.why: The last tax lever. It pays for itself only at a large, profitable prison.

nodes.name: Credit Line
nodes.summary: Borrow against your credit rating.
nodes.why: Building a wing before the contract advance arrives is usually correct. Interest is hourly, so repay it actively.

nodes.name: Additional Contract
nodes.summary: Hold three contracts at once instead of two.
nodes.why: Contract advances are the cheapest money in the game and this is the cheapest node that gets you more of them.

nodes.name: Land Purchase
nodes.summary: Buy the unowned parcels around your prison.
nodes.why: You will run out of room before you run out of inmates, and an unowned parcel is also an escape destination.
